Recent weeks at $10.81 show a median of 40 units (x1.14 vs baseline), but this includes a seasonal ramp and a one-time spike. The competitor opening across the street is a new, untested demand risk. Past price increases (10.81) show no consistent lift; instead, sales dropped to 31 units the following week. The noise-adjusted effect of price hikes is near x1.0. STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 35.2 | 5%-95%: 20.0 - 56.8 | 10%-90%: 22.2 - 54.0

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-44% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
